title: Geminid Meteor Shower
visibility: Worldwide, best from the Northern Hemisphere after about 10 p.m.
summary: Often the strongest shower of the year. The meteors come from debris left by the asteroid 3200 Phaethon. Approximate peak date.

title: Quadrantid Meteor Shower
summary: A short, sharp peak that only lasts a few hours, so timing matters. Approximate peak date.

title: Annular Solar Eclipse
visibility: Ring of fire in parts of South America and Africa (Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Brazil, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Togo, Benin, Nigeria). Partial over a wider area.
summary: The Moon passes in front of the Sun but is too far from Earth to cover it fully, leaving a bright ring around its edge.

title: Penumbral Lunar Eclipse
visibility: Depends on location. Check a local eclipse calculator.
summary: The Moon passes through the faint outer part of Earth's shadow, so it only dims slightly.

title: Lyrid Meteor Shower
visibility: Best from the Northern Hemisphere, after midnight.
summary: One of the oldest recorded meteor showers, made of debris from Comet Thatcher. Approximate peak date.

title: Eta Aquariid Meteor Shower
visibility: Best from the Southern Hemisphere, before dawn.
summary: Fast meteors from dust left by Halley's Comet. Approximate peak date.

title: Total Solar Eclipse
visibility: Total in southern Spain, North Africa (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt), Saudi Arabia and Yemen. Partial in most of Europe, the Middle East and eastern Canada.
summary: The Moon completely covers the Sun for several minutes along a narrow path, turning day into twilight.

title: Perseid Meteor Shower
visibility: Northern Hemisphere, best in the hours before dawn.
summary: A summer favorite with many bright meteors, caused by debris from Comet Swift-Tuttle. Approximate peak date.

title: Penumbral Lunar Eclipse
visibility: Depends on location. Check a local eclipse calculator.
summary: A subtle eclipse where the Moon slips through the outer edge of Earth's shadow.

title: Orionid Meteor Shower
summary: A second shower from Halley's Comet debris, known for fast meteors. Approximate peak date.

title: Geminid Meteor Shower
visibility: Worldwide, best from the Northern Hemisphere after about 10 p.m.
summary: The year's strongest shower returns. Approximate peak date.

title: Partial Lunar Eclipse
visibility: Depends on location. Check a local eclipse calculator.
summary: Part of the Moon moves into Earth's dark inner shadow and looks like a bite has been taken out of it.

title: Annular Solar Eclipse
visibility: Depends on location. Check a local eclipse calculator.
summary: Another ring of fire eclipse, where the Moon leaves a thin ring of the Sun showing.
